name: How sure the atlas is: its noise, beaten down by averaging

layers.name: how sure the atlas is, every site
layers.key_html:
Color key
dark: noise 0.0017 or less (sure)bright: 0.0172 or more (least sure)
The noise is in methylation (0 to 1). Each doubling of the draws dims every site by the same step, so what stays lit longest is where the atlas is least sure. Charcoal: no site there, or the X and Y hidden.
layers.hint: Slide right to average more draws: sure sites go dark first; the least sure stay lit to the end.
layers.fixed: How sure the atlas is at each site: the noise left in an average of k draws. Median spread 0.0029 on the autosomes, 0.0105 on the X and Y.
layers.note: Each frame is the site's posterior spread (from the atlas's 95 % range) over the square root of the number of draws averaged. The X and Y stay lit longest: the atlas's donors are women and men, and a woman holds one X methylated.

about: IAM-Atlas v2.1 was fitted the way a sky map is: every site carries 100 equally likely versions of each cell's healthy map (posterior draws, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.23422688). Averaging more draws beats the noise down, about as one over the square root of their number, which is how the microwave sky's noise is beaten down by more observing. Slide from 1 draw to 100: sure places go dark first, and what stays lit longest is where the atlas is least sure. Why it is here: before trusting a change a sample shows against the atlas, check that the atlas is sure at that place.
